questions.question: While troubleshooting a 600 V panel, you find the disconnect is off but your meter still reads voltage on one phase. What is the safest next action?
options: Continue because the disconnect is off
Stop and identify the source of voltage
Touch the conductor with an insulated screwdriver
questions.explanation: Equipment must be proven de-energized before work begins. Unexpected voltage may indicate backfeed, stored energy, or incorrect isolation.

questions.category: Task 2: Uses Tools and Equipment — 2 Questions
questions.question: A clamp meter is placed around all three phase conductors of a balanced motor feeder and reads almost zero. Why?
questions.explanation: Equal three-phase currents produce magnetic fields that cancel when clamped together. To measure current, clamp around one conductor only.

questions.question: A one-line diagram shows a 75 kVA transformer, but the equipment schedule lists 45 kVA. What is the correct action?
questions.explanation: Transformer size affects feeders, protection, and load capacity. Conflicting documents must be clarified before work proceeds.

questions.category: Task 4: Fabricates and Installs Support Components — 2 Questions
questions.question: A cable tray support is installed with inadequate anchoring for the load. What is the main concern?
questions.explanation: Support systems must carry the weight of cables and equipment safely. Poor anchoring can cause collapse, cable damage, and injury.

questions.category: Task 5: Commissions and Decommissions Electrical Systems — 2 Questions
questions.question: Before energizing a new three-phase motor circuit, what should be verified?
questions.explanation: Incorrect phase rotation can damage motor-driven equipment. Insulation testing helps confirm conductors and motor windings are safe.
